subject: QueensBay: latency + 5xx spiral in us-west — immediate mitigation & exec attention
messages:
From: Lina Torres <lina@queensbay.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.example
Date: Wed, 23 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: URGENT: platform latency + 5xx spike (us-west)

Olga —

We’re seeing a sudden, sustained spike from ~09:05 PST across our prod traffic to your us-west AZ. Key observables: p50 ~ 450ms (normal), p95 ~ 1.2s -> 2.7s, p99 spiked to ~3.1s. 5xx rate at the edge is ~4.7% for the last 10 minutes. Throughput is backing off; our client-side timeouts are firing and some jobs are failing end-to-end.

This is impacting our checkout flow (checkout rate down ~18% vs baseline) and a handful of high-value requests timed out. We need immediate mitigation and a clear ETA for resolution. Can you:
- Fail traffic away from the impacted AZ/region (prefer eastus2) or provide a safe manual reroute?
- Share any quick mitigations you can apply now (capacity bump, canary swap, rollback)?
- Confirm whether this will result in credits; we’ll need guidance on the claims process.

I’ve attached a small sample of logs around the errors and a screenshot of our dashboard.

Attached: request_log_samples.json.gz, perf_screenshot.png

—
Lina Torres
Director of Engineering, QueensBay Media
lina@queensbay.com
support@queensbay.com

Date: Wed, 23 May 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: URGENT: platform latency + 5xx spike (us-west)

Thanks Lina — I see the alerts and I’m escalating immediately. I’m looping in Incident Response (Hannah) and Support (Vanessa) to run the failover playbook and confirm mitigations.

Immediate next steps we are taking now:
- IR to validate whether this is an AZ-specific kernel/host degradation vs a routing/queueing amplification.
- If AZ-local, we will trigger a controlled regional redirection (canary first) to eastus2.
- Increasing dedicated pool capacity for QueensBay temporarily while we stabilize.

We’ll post a status update in the next 20–30 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — we’re treating this as a P0.

—
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.example
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.example
To: olga_petrov@redwood.example, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example, rishi_malhotra@redwood.example
Date: Wed, 23 May 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: URGENT: platform latency + 5xx spike (us-west) — actions taken

Olga/Team —

Triage summary: we confirmed a surge in queue wait times on a subset of us-west inference hosts combined with elevated kernel-level soft lock contention after a recent maintenance window. This is manifesting as head-of-line amplification under specific request size patterns (large-seq batching).

Actions executed (09:35–10:02 PST):
- Activated runbook "regional-evacuation-temp-redirect" (see attached canary_rollout_plan.md).
- Initiated 30% canary redirect of inbound traffic for QueensBay to eastus2 (no model variant change).
- Scaled up QueensBay dedicated pool by +25% (cold start pressure observed but acceptable for immediate relief).
- Enabled additional logging at ingress and turned off a non-critical batching optimization that was exacerbating the kernel contention.

Preliminary results: canary traffic shows error rate down from 4.7% -> 0.6% and p99 falling toward ~950ms on redirected traffic. us-west remaining traffic still elevated but improving; we will increase redirection to 70% if metrics continue to trend.

Attachment: canary_rollout_plan.md

We recommend: keep canary at 30% for 15 minutes to validate, then step to 70% with a rapid rollback if any regression.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Incident Response — Redwood Inference
From: olga_petrov@redwood.example
To: Lina Torres <lina@queensbay.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.example, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example
Date: Wed, 23 May 2028 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Update: QueensBay incident (us-west) — mitigation in progress

Hi Lina —

Quick update from our side: we activated a controlled canary redirect to eastus2 and scaled your reserved pool. Early numbers look promising — redirected requests have an error rate ~0.6% and p99 <1s. We’re holding at 30% canary to validate stability and will step to 70% within 15–20 minutes if there are no regressions.

What we’re doing next:
- Continue phased traffic shift and monitor key customer flows (checkout).
- Forensics: we’ll bundle host-level traces and ingress logs and upload to the shared Drive link.
- Post-incident: we’ll propose a credit for the impacted window; please confirm the billing contact for the claim.

Status link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/SUP-4321
Attached: status_snapshot.txt

If you want an exec-level update call, I can schedule Rishi (Director, Customer Success) and Hannah to join — please let me know availability.

—
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: olga_petrov@redwood.example
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example, sean_gallagher@redwood.example
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.example, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example
Date: Wed, 23 May 2028 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: EXTERNAL ESCALATION: QueensBay — exec outreach & credit approval

Rishi/Sean —

QueensBay remains impacted this morning with a P0 that has been partially mitigated via phased canary redirection to eastus2 (see notes above). Customer impact: checkout throughput down ~12% during the 09:05–10:20 PST window; high-value transactions affected. Customer is requesting exec outreach and guidance on credits.

Asks: 
1) Can we approve a preliminary service credit of 20% for the impacted billing day's usage while we finish forensics? If you want a different figure I’m open to guidance but they’ve flagged revenue impact.
2) Rishi — can you join a 30-minute executive briefing with Lina (they asked for an exec touchpoint) this afternoon (I suggested 16:30 PST)?
3) Sean — CS would like a short customer-facing note we can share that summarizes root-cause hypothesis and next steps (for Lina’s execs).

I’ll keep the SUP-4321 ticket updated and upload forensics to the Drive link as soon as Hannah finalizes traces.

Thanks —
Olga
